'I will put My Spirit on Him' (Isa 42:1); 'I will put My Spirit on Him' (Matt 12:18).
'he came and lived in a city called Nazareth ... He will be called a Nazarene' (Matt 2:23).

'they will call Him Immanuel” (which means, “God with us”)' (Matt 1:23). The verse says 'his name' and the child is named Jesus two verses earlier (Matt 1:21), so joining them is the graph's step -- a short one, since it is one sentence about one child.
'out of Egypt I called My son' (Hos 11:1).

Matthew applies it to the children killed at Bethlehem, and Rachel was buried 'on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem)' (Gen 35:19). The geographic join is the graph's; neither verse makes it.; 'on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem)' (Gen 35:19), and Matthew applies the lament to the children of that town.
'Rachel weeping for her children' (Jer 31:15); 'Rachel weeping for her children' (Matt 2:18). The corpus spells her name both ways.; Named in the lament, and she is buried on the road to Bethlehem.
The citation follows immediately on Judas returning the money (Matt 27:3-5) and does not name him. Implied for that reason alone.
The town is named in the saying itself, both times.
'O Daughter of Zion' (Zech 9:9); 'the Daughter of Zion' (Matt 21:5).
